messages:
maria: heads-up — ran a perfetto + nvprof sweep on canary-2026-03 with the mixed-seqlen load. seeing short HBM BW bursts (to ~880GB/s) that align with long kernel queueing and a KV read miss storm when seq >= 4096.
aj: upload the traces? rough p50/p95 numbers?
maria: pushing links now. trace (perfetto): https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 — nvprof summary attached. p50 gen latency stable ~48ms but p95 jumps to 420ms in bursts. GPU util at ~85% but big stalls on memcpy + kernel launch queues.
maria: exact repro: `./bench --model guppy-13b --seq-len-dist skewed --microbatch 4 --use-kv-cache`
maria: nvprof snippet:```Kernel Name                          Time(ms)  Calls
fused_attn_qk_kernel                 1.2       5400
kv_read_batch                        3.9       720
merge_kv_page                        0.6       720
memcpy_h2d                           0.9       48
```
lee: interesting that `kv_read_batch` is heavier — could be prefetch mispredictions. did you enable the new windowed-LRU?
maria: yes, windowed-LRU is on default window=1024. when i lower window to 256 the HBM bursts smooth out but tail latency goes up overall (more misses).
nina: that smells like a contention vs miss-rate tradeoff. long sequences inflate the KV read working set and the prefetcher starts issuing lots of async copies that saturate HBM.
perf-bot: aggregated stats from traces: {"hbmburst_pct": "0.18", "max_bw_gb_s": "882", "mean_gpu_util": "85", "memcpy_stall_ms": "320"} (report auto-generated) :robot_face:
aj: can you diff traces vs the last good canary? PR 4921 changed the kernel selection fallback to prefer `fused_attn_qk_v2` for short seqs — maybe that changed the queueing behavior for mixed loads.
maria: opened a comparison: https://github.com/redwood/inference/compare/canary-2026-02...canary-2026-03 — i see that the new selector inserts an extra `sync_stream()` on some paths which appears as blocking cudaEvent waits in perfetto.
lee: extra syncs will amplify microbatch tailing. maybe rewrite selector to avoid forcing host sync for kv-prefetch path.
nina: another datapoint — on H100 we saw ~1.8x more memcpy concurrency but same issue at high seq variance. roofline points to bandwidth bound for kv_read_batch. suggestion: throttle prefetch concurrency by inflight prefetches cap per-GPU.
maria: tried naive cap=8 prefetches and the p95 dropped from 420ms -> 190ms, bursts down to ~520GB/s. overall throughput reduced ~6%, but much smoother latency.
aj: good short-term mitigation. for longer-term we should: 1) remove sync in selector 2) implement prefetch backpressure 3) add a seq-aware batching heuristic that groups similar seq lengths to reduce working set spikes.
lee: i can prototype backpressure in the runtime request scheduler. probably add token-budget per-GPU and only issue prefetches while budget > threshold.
nina: can we surface a console metric for "kv-prefetch-inflight" and HBM-bandwidth so customers can see this interaction?
maria: yes — adding a tracing tag and dashboard panel. also will attach perfetto timeline with annotated kernel lanes to the PR.
perf-bot: perf regression alert: p95 gen latency +170ms compared to baseline canary-2026-02 (regression id: prf-20260318-71).
aj: flagging on the perf regression board + assigning eng-runtime. cc @lee @nina.
lee: quick question — any sign of page thrash at the driver level (nvml logs)?
maria: nvml sampling shows occasional page_fault_counters rising during bursts, but not enough to indicate full thrash. more like repeated big DMA ops.
nina: ok — next steps: (1) PR to remove syncs from selector (maria) (2) runtime prefetch backpressure prototype (lee) (3) dashboard + perfetto annotations (maria) (4) run a long 24h mixed-seqlen soak with modified prefetch params (aj).
maria: will draft the PR and attach annotated perfetto + nvprof exports. thanks all :thumbsup:
aj: thanks — schedule a quick sync if the 24h soak reproduces sustained regressions.
maria: will update thread with soak link later.
